subject: biology
title: Discovery and development of drugs
key_idea: Drugs were traditionally extracted from plants and microorganisms, but most new drugs are now made by chemists. Every new drug is tested for toxicity, efficacy and dose, first in the laboratory and then in clinical trials, before it can be used.

blocks.text: Many drugs were first found in living things. Today most new drugs are made in the pharmaceutical industry.

items: Traditionally, drugs were extracted from plants and microorganisms.
Most new drugs are **synthesised** by chemists in the pharmaceutical industry.
The starting point may still be a chemical extracted from a plant.
Foxgloves, willow and Penicillium mould gave us digitalis, aspirin and penicillin.
Most new drugs are now synthesised by chemists.

sections.heading: Testing and trialling a new drug

blocks.text: New drugs must be tested to check that they are safe and effective before they are used on patients. The tests look at three things.

items.meaning: Whether the drug is poisonous or harmful to the body.
Whether the drug works, that is, whether it treats the disease.
How much of the drug is needed.
A dummy treatment that contains no active drug.

items: After discovery, a new drug goes through a development phase before testing.
Done in a laboratory using cells (in vitro), tissues and live animals.
It checks whether the drug is safe and works before it is given to people.
Use healthy volunteers and patients.
A very low dose is given at the start, to check the drug is safe.
If it is safe, further trials find the optimum dose and test whether the drug works.
In a **double blind trial**, some patients are given a placebo. Neither the patients nor the doctors know who has the drug and who has the placebo.
A placebo group acts as a comparison, to check the drug works and to remove any psychological effect.

diagram.alt: Put the stages of developing a new drug in order, from discovery to publication of the results.
diagram.prompt: Put the stages of developing a new drug in the correct order.
steps: A new drug is discovered or synthesised
Preclinical testing on cells, tissues and live animals
Clinical trial begins with a very low dose in healthy volunteers
Further trials in patients find the optimum dose and test efficacy, including a double blind trial with a placebo
Results are published after peer review

items: Drugs are tested for toxicity, efficacy and dose.
Preclinical testing comes first, then clinical trials on healthy volunteers and patients.
A double blind trial uses a placebo, and neither patients nor doctors know who has the drug.

blocks.text: The results of testing and trials are only published after scrutiny by other scientists. This is called peer review.

items: Peer review helps to detect false claims.
Other scientists check the methods and conclusions before the results are published.
Results are published only after peer review.
Peer review helps to detect false claims.

checks.q: Name the plant that the heart drug digitalis comes from.
Give three reasons why a new drug must be tested before it is used.
checks.a: To check it is not toxic (poisonous or harmful), to check its efficacy (that it works), and to find the correct dose.

checks.q: Explain why a placebo group is used in a clinical trial.
checks.a: It acts as a control, for comparison, to check the drug itself works and to remove any psychological effect.

worked_example.question:
A new treatment has been shown to be effective in the laboratory using both infected tissue culture cells and infected live animals. The treatment is now ready for clinical trials on people.

Describe how the clinical trials should be carried out.
answer_points: It is given first to healthy volunteers, at a very low dose, to test it is safe (toxicity) or to check for side effects.
It is then given to some patients with the disease.
This tests for the correct (optimum) dose and checks for side effects.
It tests for efficacy, or whether it works.
It is a double blind trial, where neither patients nor doctors know who has the treatment and who has a placebo.
A large trial, a long duration or control variables.
worked_example.tip: This is a levelled question. Cover healthy volunteers first, then patients, with a reason for each stage.

worked_example.question:
New antibiotics are being developed to treat the disease caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae.

Describe the stages of antibiotic development that would occur after the discovery of a new antibiotic.
answer_points: The antibiotic would go through a development phase.
Pre-clinical stage: testing on animals, in vitro or on cells.
Clinical stage: testing on (healthy) volunteers and on patients.
Double-blind trials (a placebo and the drug).
worked_example.tip: Any three of these points score one mark each. Named animals are accepted.

worked_example.question:
Doctors are trying to find a treatment to prevent migraines. They have produced an antibody against a protein in the brain. The doctors test the antibody treatment on migraine patients. The patients are divided into two groups:

- One group is given an injection of the antibody
- The second group receives an injection of a placebo.

Explain why a placebo group is used in drug testing.
answer_points: The placebo group is a control.
It acts as a comparison, to check the drug works (to see the effects of the drug).
It identifies or eliminates any psychological effect, because some people believe they feel better when they are not.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each point. A placebo contains no active drug.
